The test image shows soybean plants with some lower leaf yellowing/browning and small spots on leaves. The upper canopy is mostly green while lower leaves show yellowing and some necrosis. This is a whole-plant/leaf view. Key candidates: Septoria brown spot (lower canopy, small dark brown spots), Sudden death syndrome (interveinal necrosis), or Soybean Vein necrosis virus.

Let me check a Septoria brown spot reference.

The reference image for Septoria brown spot shows dark brown/black spots with yellow halos on lower canopy leaves — matching the test image's pattern of lower-leaf yellowing with scattered spots while the upper canopy remains green. The field setting and soil type also match.

The test image shows:
- Lower leaf yellowing and necrosis while upper canopy stays green
- Small scattered spots/lesions on leaves
- Overall mild-to-moderate disease progression from lower canopy upward

This fits Septoria brown spot well: disease initiates in the lower canopy, small irregularly shaped dark brown lesions coalesce causing yellowing and defoliation of lower/middle canopy.
